alternatives.name: Fidelity ZERO Total Market
alternatives.rationale: FZROX offers the broadest US equity exposure at zero cost, making it ideal as a single core holding for hands-off investors seeking market-weight returns across all capitalizations. Caveat: Fidelity-only portability means you cannot transfer shares to another brokerage.

alternatives.name: Fidelity 500 Index
alternatives.rationale: FXAIX tracks the S&P 500 at near-zero cost and serves investors who want large-cap US equity exposure with perfect liquidity and portability across brokers. Caveat: It excludes mid- and small-cap stocks, so it is narrower than a total-market fund.

alternatives.name: Schwab US Dividend Equity
alternatives.rationale: SCHD focuses on quality dividend-paying US large-caps, appealing to income-seekers and investors who favor lower volatility and defensive characteristics. Caveat: It structurally underweights growth and technology sectors, so it will lag when those areas lead.

alternatives.name: Vanguard Total International Stock
alternatives.rationale: VXUS delivers comprehensive non-US equity diversification across developed and emerging markets, reducing home-country concentration risk for US-centric portfolios. Caveat: International stocks have lagged US equities for over a decade, testing the patience of many investors.

alternatives.name: Avantis US Small Cap Value
alternatives.rationale: AVUV targets US small-cap value stocks with quality and profitability screens, suiting investors willing to accept higher volatility for potential long-term factor premiums. Caveat: Small-value can underperform for years during growth-led markets, and the 0.25% fee is higher than passive cap-weighted alternatives.

alternatives.name: Invesco Nasdaq-100
alternatives.rationale: QQQM concentrates in the 100 largest Nasdaq stocks (heavily tech and growth), fitting investors who want explicit large-cap growth and innovation exposure. Caveat: Sector concentration and momentum-driven volatility mean sharper drawdowns when growth falls out of favor.

alternatives.name: Vanguard Total Bond Market
alternatives.rationale: BND holds investment-grade US bonds across maturities, providing ballast and income while dampening portfolio volatility for risk-averse or near-term savers. Caveat: Bond returns are modest and vulnerable to rising interest rates, limiting upside compared to equities.

alternatives.name: iShares Core Growth (60/40)
alternatives.rationale: AOR is a single-ticket 60/40 global stock/bond allocation, simplifying rebalancing for investors who want a moderate-risk balanced portfolio without ongoing maintenance. Caveat: Fixed 60/40 weighting may not match your specific risk tolerance, and the wrapper adds a layer of fees over holding components directly.

alt_intro: Rather than chasing last year's standout performers, consider building around a low-cost core equity fund, then layering in complementary exposures—international, factors, or bonds—based on your risk capacity and desire for diversification. One-year results reflect recent market conditions (large-cap tech dominance), not the reliability or suitability of each strategy over a full market cycle.
